summary: Intermittent high tail latency and 504s caused by ELB TCP write-backpressure saturating accept queues and queuing inference requests
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NovaHealth, dedicated) started reporting intermittent spikes in end-to-end inference latency and a small number of 504s during long streaming completions. The pattern is tail-only (95th/99th percentile), primarily during bursts of concurrent requests from the customer's integration.

Impact:
- Multiple user-facing features in NovaHealth degraded (chat and clinical note-generation pipelines).
- Approx 1-3% of requests returned 504 during peak bursts, with many more exhibiting >1s TTFB increases.
- Incident window observed 2026-03-12 03:00–07:30 UTC with smaller recurrences afterwards.

Environment:
- Customer on Dedicated capacity in us-west-2.
- Ingress fronted by internal ELB (NLB+proxy layer) then internal API Gateway.
- Serving runtime nodes: c5g-large-like GPU fleet (private dedicated pool) running redwood-v1-13b.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Customer sends 50 concurrent streaming requests with ~1200 token completions each using chunked transfer.
2. After ~30s into steady state, we observe accept queue growth on several serving nodes and zero bytes sent from upstream to customer for 1–2s bursts.
3. Upstream health checks remain green; new TCP connections succeed but per-connection write stalls increase.

Observed behavior:
- ELB shows per-target active connections saturating and TCP retransmits increase.
- Kernel send queue on ingress proxies grows; write() syscalls start returning EAGAIN more frequently.
- Serving runtime reports request queues building (head-of-line queuing) leading to increased inference latency and occasional gateway 504s when proxy-level request timeouts are reached.

Expected behavior:
- Serving runtime should maintain steady acceptance of requests with internal backpressure mechanisms and not experience ELB-level TCP write backpressure that causes broad request queueing.

Logs/metrics excerpts:
- ELB target active connections: spike from 90 -> 480 between 03:42-03:44 UTC
- Kernel tcp_retransmit_skb count: +3.2k in 5 min on proxy-az2
- Serving runtime accept queue length metric (accept_queue_len): increased from 2 to 18 on affected nodes
- Sample proxy dmesg: "tcp_sendmsg: EAGAIN - returned without sending"

Temporary impact mitigation timeline:
- 2026-03-12 05:10 UTC: shifted affected customer traffic to alternate ELB pool (reduced immediate error rate).
- 2026-03-12 05:35 UTC: increased per-proxy ulimit and adjusted net.core.wmem_max temporarily on a subset of nodes.

Notes: this looks distinct from header-bloat cases — packet-level retransmits and kernel send queue saturation point to TCP-level backpressure in the ELB/proxy path rather than HTTP header growth or HPACK issues.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis was large request headers; packet capture showed normal header sizes but increasing TCP retransmits.
Reproduced increased accept_queue_len locally under synthetic load that simulates many simultaneous streaming responses where downstream read windows shrink.
Observed correlation between ELB target_active_connections and host-level send buffer exhaustion on proxy instances.
Checked ALB/NLB configuration: connection_reuse_timeout at default, target group deregistration time default (no aggressive drain configured).
Kernel tuning changes (wmem_max) on a canary set reduced EAGAIN frequency but not eliminated the effect under highest load.
No serving-runtime OOMs or model hangs observed; CPU/GPUs healthy — this is a network egress bottleneck.
Related issues about proxy buffering and idle timeouts (SUP-77412, SUP-91827) noted; however those focused on header-induced idle resets rather than sustained TCP-level backpressure.
comments: 2026-03-12 06:02 UTC - Damian Cole (Support): Thanks for the signal, Aisha. We're prioritizing the network path and have moved NovaHealth to a different ELB pool. Can you provide recent pcap and kernel tcp_sndbuf metrics?
2026-03-12 06:17 UTC - Aisha Patel (Customer Success): Uploaded pcap to S3: s3://support-artifacts/SUP-27644/pcap-03-12.pcap. Customer confirms degraded UX during the window.

2026-03-12 06:45 UTC - SRE oncall (Sofia Martinez): Canary hosts updated net.core.wmem_max=12582912 and raised file descriptor ulimits; saw EAGAIN drop ~40% on canary. Policy: don't roll cluster-wide until we validate.

2026-03-13 09:10 UTC - Network (Ethan Kim): NLB health shows increased retransmits to proxy AZ2; opening infra PR to add more aggressive connection reuse and increase tx buffer defaults. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/8923

2026-03-14 11:30 UTC - Damian Cole (Support): Customer verifies error rate reduced but occasional tail spikes remain during extreme bursts. Engineering to evaluate long-term fixes (ELB config + kernel tuning + serving runtime read-window backpressure).
resolution: Mitigation applied: moved customer to alternative ELB pool and applied kernel send-buffer increases on ingress proxies; temporary reduction in error rate and tail latency. Next steps: infra will propose ELB configuration changes (increase connection reuse and adjust flow control timeouts) and SRE/Serving to add explicit downstream read-window awareness in runtime to avoid large bursts. Follow-up action item: infra PR (github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/8923) and a targeted rollout to all ingress proxies after validation. Incident remains open until rollouts complete and 7 days of stable telemetry are observed.
